;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Libya–Turkey relations]]
**[[Turkey|Turkish]] [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces he will send [[Turkish Armed Forces|troops]] to [[Libya]] to help the internationally-recognized [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]-based [[Government of National Accord]] after they requested support. He plans to submit his motion to the [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey|Grand National Assembly]] on January 7 for approval. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/erdogan-announces-plan-send-troops-libya-191226090214331.html (Al Jazeera)]  
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Fourteen [[Niger Armed Forces|Nigerien soldiers]] are killed by heavily armed militant gunmen who ambushed the convoy in the [[Tillabéri Region]] of [[Niger]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20191226-niger-authorities-say-14-troops-killed-during-ambush-g5-sahel-force-west-africa (France24)]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital punishment in Japan]]
**[[Japan]] [[Hanging#Japan|executes]] a foreigner for the first time since the disclosure of details of its sentences began in 2007. He was a [[Chinese people in Japan|Chinese]] man convicted of killing a family of four. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-deathpenalty/japan-executes-first-foreigner-in-years-a-chinese-man-who-killed-a-family-idUSKBN1YU07N (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50916494 (BBC News)]
*[[Censorship in Turkey]]
**The [[Constitutional Court of Turkey]] orders the immediate lifting of the [[block of Wikipedia in Turkey]], ruling it a [[Human rights#Violations|violation]] of the [[freedom of expression]]. In response to the news, Wikipedia co-founder [[Jimmy Wales]] says, "Welcome back, Turkey!" [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/dec/26/turkish-court-wikipedia-block-lifted (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 Ivorian general election]]
**In [[Ivory Coast]], former rebel leader, prime minister and presidential candidate for next year's general election, [[Guillaume Soro]], could face prison for life over an alleged [[coup]] plot that involved amassing weapons, says the country's public prosecutor. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ivorycoast-politics/ivory-coast-says-presidential-candidate-soro-plotted-a-coup-idUSKBN1YU14A?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A court in [[Morocco]] sentences a man to four years in prison for insulting the [[King of Morocco|king]]. Authorities also arrest a [[Twitter]] user for criticizing the long prison terms given to those who protest. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-morocco-trial/morocco-jails-one-man-detains-another-over-criticism-of-authorities-on-social-media-idUSKBN1YU16M (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Citizenship Amendment Act protests]]
**[[Chief Minister]] of [[Uttar Pradesh]] [[Yogi Adityanath]] threatens to confiscate property from more than 200 people, mostly [[Islam in India|Muslims]], allegedly to pay for damages caused by protesters. The northern [[India]]n [[States and union territories of India|state]] has seen the most violence from the protests, with 18 out of the 25 killings happening there. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/indian-state-warns-law-protesters-confiscate-property-191226111207708.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Freedom of religion in Montenegro]]
**Hundreds of protesters, mostly consisting of supporters of the pro-[[Serbia]] opposition bloc, march in [[Podgorica]], [[Montenegro]], to protest a proposed law that would require [[Religion in Montenegro|religious communities]] to provide proof of property ownership from before the [[creation of Yugoslavia]] in 1918. Protesters claim the law unfairly targets the predominant [[Serbian Orthodox Church]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-montenegro-protest/serbs-protest-in-montenegro-ahead-of-vote-on-religious-law-idUSKBN1YU0WC?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Israeli legislative election]]
**[[Israel]]i [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] survives a primary challenge from former [[Ministry of Education (Israel)|Education Minister]] [[Gideon Sa'ar]] with 72% of the vote. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/dec/26/israel-voting-under-way-in-likud-primary-seen-as-threat-to-netanyahu (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Iraqi protests]]
**[[Iraq]]i [[President of Iraq|President]] [[Barham Salih]] rejects the nomination of [[Basra Governorate|Basra]] governor [[Asaad Al Eidani]] for [[Prime Minister of Iraq]], stating that protesters will also oppose him due to his connections with [[Iran]]ian-backed [[List of political parties in Iraq|parties]]. As the [[Constitution of Iraq|constitution]] doesn't give him the power to officially veto candidates, Salih threatens to resign instead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/iraq-president-threatens-quit-pm-nominee-191226132315483.html (Al Jazeera)]
